data.G: Not assembled in this preparation phase. Start from the supplied baseline; after the research trees close, integrate only measured, correctness-validated candidates and independently confirm the resulting G.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the baseline is a scalar UTF-8 validator with an ASCII fast path, leaving three complementary hypotheses to test—whole-stream SIMD validation, SIMD-assisted ASCII skipping with scalar decoding, and scalar decoder control-flow reduction. The only supplied measurement is the valid baseline: mean 49.623 µs across three samples (score 0.5); no child candidate has been measured or confirmed. The stated one-core budget favors serial implementations, not OpenMP parallelism. Keep every change to src/candidate.cpp, preserve the run ABI and full uint32 output, and retain correctness for all input lengths and malformed UTF-8. Do not assume gains combine; measure any integration and reserve an independent confirmation of final G.

children.objective: Implement and measure a whole-buffer x86 SIMD UTF-8 validator: classify bytes and validate continuation requirements and restricted second-byte ranges with masks, correctly carry state across vector boundaries, and handle short inputs and the tail without reading beyond n. Explore only ISA code legal on the frozen EPYC 9654 target under the unchanged build protocol. Preserve exact scalar-value validity rules and the ABI/output behavior. Compare against the supplied baseline on valid mixed-width n=65536 input; also verify ASCII and malformed-input correctness. Record failed variants and measurements.
children.subject: Whole-stream SIMD UTF-8 validation with cross-block state

children.objective: Keep strict scalar code-point validation for non-ASCII data, but explore safe word/vector high-bit scans to skip long ASCII spans and dispatch to the next non-ASCII lead byte. Ensure sequences and errors at scan boundaries are handled correctly, and tails are bounded; do not rely on the test length or contents. Preserve the ABI, output, and thread budget. Measure mixed-width n=65536 performance and check ASCII and malformed correctness against the baseline; record failed attempts.
children.subject: SIMD-assisted ASCII-run skipping with a scalar slow path

children.objective: Explore pure-scalar alternatives that reduce per-code-point branch and dependency cost, such as compact byte-class/DFA logic or a reduced-branch decoder. Do not add SIMD ASCII scanning or extra threads, keeping this investigation distinct from the other trees. Preserve all UTF-8 scalar-value checks, safe bounds for every length, the ABI, full uint32 output, and the thread budget. Measure valid mixed-width n=65536 performance and verify ASCII and malformed correctness; report failures as well as wins.
children.subject: Branch-reduced scalar UTF-8 decoding
